messages:
jordan: heads-up — after flipping the `v2` default routing for new keys we started seeing a ~6% spike in 4xx errors for customers still on older sdk versions. Not all of these are real client bugs — some are strict-header/accept changes + our fallback routing returning `402/invalid-route` instead of a smooth fallback. Need a clear compatibility/fallback policy.

matt: ugh. do we have a reproduction? is it specifically `Accept`/`Content-Type` headers or path change? any sample logs? :thinking:

jordan: I pulled a few traces. Example request from older client: `POST /v1/generate` with header `Accept: application/json; charset=utf-8`. v2 routing expects `application/vnd.redwood.v2+json` and rejects. In some cases our router returns `404`/`unsupported` rather than falling back to the v1 handler. snippet from trace:```
[router] route_decision: attempted v2 -> parsing error -> NO_FALLBACK -> 404
```

alexa: that NO_FALLBACK path is surprising — we intentionally added fallthrough to v1 for header mismatch during canary. Did the canary flag change?

sam: flags unchanged. I think the issue is we tightened the header parser in the v2 ingress to be stricter for content-negotiation. Previously we treated unknown vendor types as valid and forwarded. Now we fail-fast.

mina-product: customers are seeing this and pinging CS. We should have a console-visible banner if we keep strictness. Also migrate doc + SDK note.

matt: proposal: revert strict failure to previous permissive behavior for 90 days (shim), emit telemetry metric `compatibility.fallback_rate.v1` and `compat_failing_clients` with hashed client-version string, and add a console banner + rollout ux checkbox for opt-in strict v2 parsing.

alexa: agree with telemetry and banner. For the shim period: 90 days is fine but we need config knobs: `router.accept_strictness = permissive | strict` per-tenant, default permissive for older keys. Also we should add an access log field `client_sdk_version` (best-effort from UA/header) so we can drive outreach.

jordan: timeline-wise: revert parser change on router (hotfix) today, add telemetry + access-log change in next week, then start deprecation notices in console at +30 days, and remove shim at +90 days. Who owns the router revert?

sam: I can revert the parser and push a canary now. Will mark the change with `revert: permissive-parse` in deploy. Need an owner to watch error drift for 48h.

matt: i'll monitor and create a simple dashboard (per-model, per-route) showing `4xx_rate`, `compatibility.fallback_rate.v1`, and `client_sdk_version` breakdown. I'll add alert if fallback_rate > 2% for 24h.

alexa: UX note — in Console rollout flow we should show a warning card if a customer toggles `strict v2` and their `client_sdk_versions` coverage is <95%. Also include a link to a migration guide and a quick `curl` example to detect behavior: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate -H 'Accept: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -i
```

mina-product: I'll draft the console banner copy: "API versioning update: v2 header parsing will become strict on YYYY-MM-DD. Customers using older SDKs will continue to be routed to v1 for 90 days; update your SDK or follow the migration guide."

sam: added to canary now. router shows revert flag active. watchers: @matt and @sre-bot please keep an eye.

sre-bot: [incident-bot] Watch started: router-permissive-parse-hotfix. Alert channel #eng-oncall. Sampling logs for 12h.

matt: noted. I'll post the dashboard link once available. Action items summary: 1) sam — revert parser (in progress) + deploy canary (owner) 2) matt — dashboard + alerts (owner) 3) jordan/mina — console banner + migration copy (owner) 4) alexa — add per-tenant `accept_strictness` flag + access-log field (owner) 5) eng-platform — schedule removal of shim in 90 days and communication plan.

jordan: thanks. one more edge-case: quotas. if we fall back to v1 handler some requests may hit different rate limits/quotas. We need to ensure fallback doesn't double-count or bypass per-route quota semantics.

alexa: good catch. router should preserve original route metadata and apply the original quota bucket. If we can't map, fallback must fail closed. I'll add a small mapping table in the router config and a test.

sam: will validate quota behaviour in canary. If we see anomalies, we'll temporarily return 429 with clear `Retry-After` so clients can backoff.

mina-product: I'll coordinate CS outreach for customers with >1% error spike and include migration steps + SDK bump link.

jordan: perfect. leaving this thread open until canary stable. ping here with dashboard link and first 24h metrics. :thumbsup:
